name: Marie Curie
hook: Two Nobels, two elements and a first at the Sorbonne — the scientist Jeopardy loves.

facts.label: Warsaw
facts.statement: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867, when the Polish capital was under Russian control.

facts.label: two Nobel Prizes
facts.statement: She was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes: Physics in 1903 with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, then Chemistry in 1911.

facts.label: polonium and radium
facts.statement: In 1898 the Curies discovered polonium, named for Marie's homeland, and radium, the element that made her famous.

facts.label: radioactivity
facts.statement: Marie Curie coined the word radioactivity for the property shown by elements such as uranium and thorium.

facts.label: the Sorbonne
facts.statement: After Pierre died, Marie took his professorship in 1906 and became the first woman to teach at the Sorbonne in Paris.

facts.label: the Panthéon
facts.statement: In 1995 she became the first woman honored in France's Panthéon in her own right.

facts.label: Irène Joliot-Curie
facts.statement: Her daughter Irène Joliot-Curie also won a Nobel in chemistry, sharing it with her husband Frédéric Joliot.
